items.readable_text:
Content:
Imagine that the [MATH: x]-axis below is a mirror. What would be the coordinates of the point [MATH: P(-4,{\color{blue}2})] after it's reflected in the [MATH: x]-axis mirror?

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/cc4111e27038b0f919e4b66478c839b9]

Content:
To reflect a point in an axis, we can use the following two steps:

Content:
1. First, move the point onto the mirror axis.
2. Then, move the same distance again on the other side of the axis.

Content:
The point [MATH: P] has coordinates [MATH: (-4,{\color{blue}{2}}).] So, to reflect [MATH: P] in the [MATH: x]-axis, we

Content:
- move it [MATH: {\color{blue}{2}}] units down to reach the [MATH: x]-axis, and then
- move it [MATH: {\color{blue}{2}}] units down again on the other side of the axis.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/3f3ba9da7991d83d423461ccccd08cae]

Content:
The resulting point [MATH: P'] has coordinates [MATH: (-4,{\color{blue}{-2}}).]

sections.normalized_html:
The point [MATH: A] has coordinates [MATH: ({\color{blue}{3}} , 2).]

Method 1

To reflect the point [MATH: A] in the [MATH: y]-axis, we move it [MATH: {\color{blue}{3}}] units left, and then [MATH: {\color{blue}{3}}] units left again.

The resulting point [MATH: B] has coordinates [MATH: (-{\color{blue}{3}} , 2).]

To reflect the resulting point [MATH: B] in the [MATH: y]-axis, we move it [MATH: {\color{blue}{3}}] units right, and then [MATH: {\color{blue}{3}}] units right again.

Note that after the double reflection in the [MATH: y]-axis, we return to the initial point [MATH: A.] It has coordinates [MATH: ({\color{blue}{3}} , 2).]

Method 2

To reflect [MATH: A] point in the [MATH: y]-axis, we change the sign of its [MATH: x]-coordinate:

[MATH: ({\color{blue}{3}} , 2) \longrightarrow (-{\color{blue}{3}} , 2)]

To reflect reflect the resulting point in the [MATH: y]-axis again, we again change the sign of its [MATH: x]-coordinate: [MATH: (-{\color{blue}{3}} , 2) \longrightarrow ({\color{blue}{3}} , 2)]

After the double reflection in the [MATH: y]-axis, we return to the initial point [MATH: A({\color{blue}{3}} , 2).]

Item 8 — Tutorial: Reflecting Points by Changing the Sign of the Other Coordinate

Content:
You may have noticed that when we reflect a point in an axis, the corresponding coordinate remains the same, while the sign of the other coordinate is changed.

Content:
In general, changing the sign of the other coordinate is a quicker method of reflecting points! To illustrate, consider the point [MATH: P] from before.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/d35996ab4f86a11d4d8c9ef39c0fda22]

Content:
To reflect [MATH: P] in the [MATH: x]-axis, we can simply change the sign of the [MATH: y]-coordinate. This gives
[MATH: (-4,{\color{blue}{2}})\longrightarrow (-4,-{\color{blue}{2}}).]

Content:
Alternatively, to reflect [MATH: P] in the [MATH: y]-axis, we can simply change the sign of the [MATH: y]-coordinate. We get
[MATH: ({\color{red}-4},2)\longrightarrow ({\color{red}4},2).]

Item 9 — Example: Finding the Coordinates of a Point After Reflecting In the Same Axis Twice

Example Prompt:
The point [MATH: A(3,2)] is reflected in the [MATH: y]-axis to make a new point [MATH: B.] The point [MATH: B] is then reflected in the [MATH: y]-axis. What are the coordinates of the final point?

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
The point [MATH: A] has coordinates [MATH: ({\color{blue}{3}} , 2).]

Method 1

To reflect the point [MATH: A] in the [MATH: y]-axis, we move it [MATH: {\color{blue}{3}}] units left, and then [MATH: {\color{blue}{3}}] units left again.

[IMG: /graphics/28ff669e86e1e9bff15bb301cf26ea03]

The resulting point [MATH: B] has coordinates [MATH: (-{\color{blue}{3}} , 2).]

To reflect the resulting point [MATH: B] in the [MATH: y]-axis, we move it [MATH: {\color{blue}{3}}] units right, and then [MATH: {\color{blue}{3}}] units right again.

[IMG: /graphics/97c2fbc7fa64546a24b4e7022599fb15]

Note that after the double reflection in the [MATH: y]-axis, we return to the initial point [MATH: A.] It has coordinates [MATH: ({\color{blue}{3}} , 2).]

Method 2

To reflect [MATH: A] point in the [MATH: y]-axis, we change the sign of its [MATH: x]-coordinate:

[MATH: ({\color{blue}{3}} , 2) \longrightarrow (-{\color{blue}{3}} , 2)]

To reflect reflect the resulting point in the [MATH: y]-axis again, we again change the sign of its [MATH: x]-coordinate:
[MATH: (-{\color{blue}{3}} , 2) \longrightarrow ({\color{blue}{3}} , 2)]

After the double reflection in the [MATH: y]-axis, we return to the initial point [MATH: A({\color{blue}{3}} , 2).]
